newsitem.title: BELGIUM: BELGIAN SHORT OLOS TO DEAR DUE EXCHANGE SALES - CLB.
newsitem.headline: BELGIAN SHORT OLOS TO DEAR DUE EXCHANGE SALES - CLB.

text.p: Belgian short-maturity OLOs have become too expensive because of the large volume at the Belgian Treasury's exchange auctions, Steven Major, head of global bond research for Credit Lyonnais said on Thursday.
"The exchange auctions are distorting the front end of the yield curve, making it too expensive" Major said at a fixed income strategy seminar organised by Credit Lyonnais Belgium.
Every month the Treasury organises exchange auctions where linear bonds close to maturity can be exchanged for OLOs with expiry dates that are further away.

The newsletter of the Primary Dealers Association said earlier this week that 50 percent of the 700 billion francs worth of bonds issued in 1996 was through exchange auctions, compared to just 20 percent in 1995.
"I recommend that investors in Belgian paper switch up the curve," he said.
Major also said that the yields of Belgian and French bonds were generally too low compared to Bunds.
But he added that there still were relative value opportunities. Major recommended selling the June 2002 OLO 10 and buying the May 2006 OLO 24.
-- Geert De Clercq, Brussels Newsroom +32 2 287 6813, Fax +32 2 230 7710
